findings.title: SSE protocol docblock still advertises `details` on error events
findings.desc: The `streamLlm` JSDoc continues to document `event: error — { error: "message", details: "..." }`, but the catch block now emits only `{ error: message }`; any client written against this contract will read `undefined`.

findings.title: `errorWithDetails` payload is now unreachable
findings.desc: With `getErrorDetails` deleted, nothing in the process reads the attached `details` property, so the new comment's claim that it "remains attached ... for any in-process consumer that opts in" describes a consumer that does not exist; the OpenRouter error body is now silently discarded, removing the only diagnostic for non-2xx streaming failures.

findings.title: Exported `getAnthropicClient` renamed without compatibility alias
findings.desc: Only `streamLlm.ts` is updated in this diff; any other importer (route handlers, existing tests, mocks referencing `getAnthropicClient`) would break at build time, and the rename is not noted anywhere as a breaking change.

findings.title: Comment's stated rationale conflicts with the adjacent response
findings.desc: The comment argues `responseText` "shouldn't end up in server logs" because it derives from user source material, yet the very next statement returns a 500-char slice of it in the HTTP body, so the redaction is partial and the justification reads as stronger than the actual behavior.

findings.title: `streamLlm` SSE contract still documents a `details` field
findings.desc: The function-level JSDoc still advertises `event: error — { error: "message", details: "..." }`, but the catch block now emits only `{ error }`; clients following the doc will read an always-undefined field.

findings.title: OpenRouter stream error bodies are now completely discarded
findings.desc: `errorWithDetails` still attaches `details`, but with `getErrorDetails` removed nothing logs or reads it anywhere, so a non-2xx OpenRouter response in the streaming path leaves only "OpenRouter API error: <status>" with no way to recover the provider message — the doc comment's claim about "any in-process consumer that opts in" describes a consumer that does not exist.

findings.title: Comment's privacy rationale contradicted two lines later
findings.desc: The comment states `responseText` "shouldn't end up in server logs" because it derives from user material, yet the same handler still returns a 500-char slice in the response body; the stated protection is only partial and the comment reads as if the leak were closed.

findings.title: Test deletes API-key env vars without restoring them

findings.title: `streamLlm` JSDoc still documents the SSE contract as `event: error — { error: "message", details: "..." }`
findings.desc: The catch block now emits only `{ error }`, so the module's own protocol documentation (and any client parsing `details` from the error event) is out of date with the code.

findings.title: Provider error bodies in the streaming path are now dropped entirely
findings.desc: `errorWithDetails` still attaches `details` (OpenRouter's response body) but nothing reads it: it is neither logged nor sent over SSE, and no in-process consumer exists, so streaming OpenRouter failures (rate limits, model errors, bad payloads) are undiagnosable; the "remains attached for any in-process consumer" comment describes dead code.

findings.title: Privacy rationale in the new comment is inconsistent with the same handler's behavior
findings.desc: The comment justifies stripping content from logs as sensitive, yet the response still returns `responseText.slice(0, 500)` and the `OpenRouterError` branch below still returns `err.details` to the caller, so the data is only hidden from operators, not from the wire.

findings.title: Exported `getAnthropicClient` renamed to `makeAnthropicClient`
findings.desc: Only `streamLlm.ts` is updated in this diff; any other importer or test referencing the old exported name (it was public API) will fail to compile, and per-call construction also forgoes any client-level state/config reuse the SDK caches.
